summary.title: From Words to Wheels: Automated Style-Customized Policy Generation for Autonomous Driving
summary.authors: Xu Han, Xianda Chen, Zhenghan Cai, Pinlong Cai, Meixin Zhu, Xiaowen Chu
summary.executive_summary: Words2Wheels is a novel framework designed to automatically generate customized driving policies for autonomous vehicles based on natural language user commands. Unlike existing methods that rely on predefined styles or data-driven inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) requiring specific historical data, Words2Wheels utilizes a Style-Customized Reward Function and a Driving Style Database. By leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), the system retrieves, adapts, and generalizes driving styles to align with user preferences without needing prior driving data for the specific command. A Statistical Evaluation module ensures the generated policies match user intent by comparing metrics like speed and jerk against natural driving baselines. Experiments using the HighD dataset and human-in-the-loop evaluations demonstrate that Words2Wheels outperforms traditional models like the Intelligent Driver Model (IDM) in accuracy, generalization, and adaptability. The framework introduces a 'fuzzy memory' function to handle semantically similar commands, significantly enhancing user experience and interactivity in autonomous driving scenarios.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
Words2Wheels is a novel framework designed to automatically generate customized driving policies for autonomous vehicles based on natural language user commands. Unlike existing methods that rely on predefined styles or data-driven inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) requiring specific historical data, Words2Wheels utilizes a Style-Customized Reward Function and a Driving Style Database. By leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), the system retrieves, adapts, and generalizes driving styles to align with user preferences without needing prior driving data for the specific command. A Statistical Evaluation module ensures the generated policies match user intent by comparing metrics like speed and jerk against natural driving baselines. Experiments using the HighD dataset and human-in-the-loop evaluations demonstrate that Words2Wheels outperforms traditional models like the Intelligent Driver Model (IDM) in accuracy, generalization, and adaptability. The framework introduces a 'fuzzy memory' function to handle semantically similar commands, significantly enhancing user experience and interactivity in autonomous driving scenarios.

Research Context
Current AVs suffer from uniform driving styles. Existing methods rely on predefined styles or IRL. Data-driven approaches struggle with data scarcity. Metrics often fail to align with user preferences. Methods are limited to pre-existing styles. Foundation models lack style-level policy adjustment.

Research Question And Hypothesis
Can we automate policy customization via NLP? Does a Style-Customized Reward Function bridge input and policy? Can LLMs generalize styles without user behavior data? Will the Statistical Evaluation module ensure alignment? Will Words2Wheels outperform existing methods? Can the system handle generalization to new commands?

Methodological Details
The study uses the HighD dataset. Data was collected by a 4K resolution camera. A 15% test set was reserved for evaluation. User commands were categorized into three levels. GPT-4o-2024-08-06 was used as the base model. Temperature was set to 0.3 for generation. k=3 styles were selected for relevance. n=2 metrics were used in Statistical Evaluation. 10 volunteers with valid licenses participated. Each volunteer tested 5 commands with 20 events each. Total of 1,000 tested events were analyzed.

Procedures And Architectures
The process starts with RAG principles. LLM selects top k relevant style rewards. Style Rewards are programming codes. Style Policies are stored as pre-trained neural networks. Proximal Policy Optimization was used for training. Training was run 5 times with different seeds. The best policy with highest reward was selected. A Chain-of-Thought approach guides metric selection. The system includes a fuzzy memory function. Backend processing runs reward generation and policy training.

Key Results
Words2Wheels outperformed IDM in human preference. 72% of events favored Words2Wheels over IDM. IDM was preferred in only 9.2% of events. Aggressive style showed higher speeds and acceleration. Conservative style maintained larger gaps. Generalization to new commands was successful. Fuzzy memory recalled similar commands successfully. Level I commands were handled with 100% rationality. System adapted to indirect hints effectively. Generated policies replaced existing ones when better.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
Style Rewards bridge user input and policy. LLMs enable zero-shot generalization. Statistical evaluation ensures objective alignment. Database expansion reduces reliance on RL. Fuzzy memory enhances adaptability to NLP. The framework shifts from data-driven to command-driven.

Contradictions And Limitations
Aggressive style had larger time headway. Normal style showed higher jerk unexpectedly. LLM sometimes misinterpreted commands. Negative acceleration values conflicted with intuition. One fuzzy memory case failed (snow). Experiments limited to car-following scenarios. Human-in-the-loop sample size was small.

Claims
Words2Wheels automatically generates customized driving policies aligned with natural language commands without requiring specific historical driving data for those commands. Generates policies without prior data. Leverages LLMs and a Driving Style Database. Generalizes to new commands effectively. Initial database requires population. Enables novel interactivity in AVs. Solves the generalization problem of IRL.
The Statistical Evaluation module ensures that generated driving styles closely align with user preferences by comparing metrics against natural driving baselines. Ensures alignment with user preferences. Prevents overfitting using a reserved test set. Uses Chain-of-Thought for metric selection. LLM sometimes selected irrelevant metrics. Provides objective style evaluation. Improves reliability of policy generation.

Data And Code Availability
Code and demo are available online. Experimental records are available via link.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Training was repeated 5 times for robustness. Ablation on command levels showed varying accuracy. Ablation on fuzzy memory showed high recall.

Key Figures Tables
Figure 1 illustrates the Words2Wheels workflow. Figure 2 shows the Driving Style Database structure. Figure 5 compares customized policies over style-aware metrics. Table II summarizes human preferences on driving style alignment. Table III presents case studies across all command levels.

Three Takeaways
1. Words2Wheels automates style customization via NLP. 2. Human evaluation confirms superiority over IDM. 3. Future work will expand to complex scenarios.
